official.application_cycle: 2027 intake, Graduate Term 1 2027 (applications open Thursday 20 August 2026, close 5pm FJT Wednesday 21 October 2026)
official.status_note: APPLICATION OPEN! Applications are invited for the 2027 intake of the PASS Scholarship Program; applications opened Thursday 20 August 2026 and close at 5pm FJT on Wednesday 21 October 2026, with scholarships available for Graduate Term 1, 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full Tuition coverage for the relevant program of study. The PASS FAQs state that Tuition and Allowances will be paid for up to 24 months for Masters students and 36 months for a PhD candidate.
benefits: Full Tuition coverage for the relevant program of study
Living Allowance (FJD$21,450 p.a. for unaccompanied & FJD$32,472 p.a. for accompanied)
Book allowance (currently FJD 750 as a one-off payment)
Establishment allowance (currently FJD 1,900, as a one-off payment, if applicable)
A Research Grant of up to a maximum of FJD17,500 for Masters' students and FJD40,000 for PhD students

The ACIAR PASS Administration team based at FNU provides additional support to PASS scholars and academic staff including professional development, peer-to-peer learning, research collaboration, and supervision training, with student work placements and career development included through the Job Ready program
eligibility: Applicants must be Pacific Island Country Nationals from ACIAR partner countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu); the FAQs state scholarships are open to current citizens of all island countries of Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu
Applicants must be 35 years or below when applying for Masters and 45 years or below for PhD. Flexibilities on the age criteria will be considered under exceptional cases
Master of Science in Agriculture (with a thesis component): a Bachelor's degree in Agriculture with a GPA of 3.0 or above
Master of Science in Forestry (with a thesis component): a Bachelor's degree in Forestry with a GPA of 3.0 or above

Masters by Research: a Postgraduate diploma with a GPA of 3.00 or above (or the equivalent from a recognised University); a bachelor's degree with a GPA of 3.5; an honours Bachelor degree with a GPA of 3.00 from a recognised institution; a Master by coursework; or recognised professional experience satisfying the Dean of the College

PhD: a Master by Research degree; where the Master degree is by coursework a GPA of minimum 4.0 is required plus completion of a research methods course; or an Honours Bachelor's degree with a GPA of minimum 4.0 and above or (First or upper Second-class Honours); or recognised professional experience satisfying the Dean of the College

The medium of instruction at FNU is the English language. Students must be sufficiently fluent in English to pursue the HDR Programme. HDR students will provide evidence from undergraduate qualifications/other English qualifications that confirm their English language competency
requirements: Check eligibility with the ACIAR Graduate Officer before applying for the scholarship
Applications, including the research intent, should be completed in consultation with the prospective supervisors at FNU and the corresponding ACIAR project leader or co-supervisor
Identify a research project from the PASS Compendium of Research Topics to pursue

All documents need to be scanned as a PDF and sent as one single attachment via email; the FAQs require the document in one PDF in the order: Application Form, Academic Transcript/s, Certificate/s, Letters of Support from proposed supervisors, Birth Certificate/Passport

The research intent is to be submitted as a separate PDF, and documents must be saved as PASS2027-your name-university-program (e.g. PASS2027Application-LisaWard-FNU-MSc) with the research intent named PASS2027ResarchIntent-your name-university-program

Applicants are required to disclose any use of AI tools or technologies in the preparation of their application, including their CV and written responses, in accordance with the PASS Information Sheet on the Use of Artificial Intelligence

For applicants already employed in the public sector, a letter confirming release of the applicant, if successful, from duties by the relevant Public Service Commission for the term of the scholarship, is a requirement
documents: Completed 2027 PASS Program Scholarship Application Form
Completed research intent including a detailed research proposal, signed by the FNU Supervisor and the ACIAR Co-supervisor (submitted as a separate PDF)
Letters of support from proposed supervisors
Written references from two referees who are familiar with you personally and in your studies, known in a professional capacity and not family members or relatives
selection_criteria: A Selection Panel at each university has been established to review the applications; applications will be assessed based on eligibility and merit
Applications will be assessed using multiple information sources: referee reports, history and academic records, and interviews or writing exercises may be conducted to verify skills
The Program aligns to ACIAR's Gender Equity Policy and Strategy, and women are particularly encouraged to apply

Each application is considered on a case-by-case basis where an applicant is already enrolled in a Masters or PhD program, provided the study is aligned with an ACIAR Project and supported by a FNU Supervisor and Co-supervisor
coverage: Full tuition coverage for the relevant program of study
Living allowance of FJD 21,450 per year (unaccompanied) or FJD 32,472 per year (accompanied / dependent allowances, if applicable)
Book allowance of FJD 750 as a one-off payment
Establishment allowance of FJD 1,900 as a one-off payment, if applicable
Medical insurance at the prevailing rate
Research grant of up to FJD 17,500 for Masters' students and FJD 40,000 for PhD students, to cover research operating costs, minor equipment, and travel expenses essential to undertake research
application_method: Check if you meet the eligibility criteria provided in the ACIAR Scholarship Application Form and confirm eligibility with the FNU ACIAR Graduate Officer
Identify a research project from the PASS Compendium of Research Topics that you wish to pursue
Contact the corresponding FNU Supervisor and relevant Co-supervisor from the list to discuss the potential research topic
Work in consultation with your FNU Supervisor and Co-supervisor to develop a sound research proposal using the Research Intent Template
Complete the application form and attach the required documents; all documents need to be scanned as a PDF and sent as one single attachment via email
Submit your application to the ACIAR Graduate and Scholarship Officer via email at aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027'
official.application_route: Email a single PDF bundle to aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027' after agreeing a topic with an FNU supervisor and ACIAR co-supervisor
official.study_mode: Full-time; students enrolled in a full-time capacity are expected to maintain a full-time study load
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be Pacific Island Country Nationals from ACIAR partner countries (Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu); the application form declaration requires the applicant to be a citizen of and currently reside in one of those countries
official.international_eligibility: Restricted to citizens of the seven listed ACIAR Pacific partner countries; nationals of other countries are not eligible to apply
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Agriculture (including horticulture), fisheries (including aquaculture) and forestry; the research topic must be selected from the ACIAR PASS Compendium of Research Topics and be aligned with an ACIAR project, with study at FNU under the College of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry
official.research_requirement: A research intent including a detailed research proposal, signed by both the FNU Supervisor and the ACIAR Co-supervisor, must be submitted as a separate PDF; the research grant is allocated based on a detailed research proposal and supporting budget prepared with the supervisor and co-supervisor
official.duration: 24 months for Masters' students and 36 months for a PhD candidate, for which tuition and allowances will be paid
official.description: ACIAR's Pacific postgraduate scholarships are offered in the Pacific, to Pacific Islanders, enabling scholars to research agricultural problems within the context that the solutions need to work, to build professional networks which will be relevant post-study and remain close to family and culture. The PASS Program aims to strengthen the Pacific agricultural innovation system through building on the strengths of Pacific universities and their regional partners, and sits within ACIAR's Pacific Capacity Building Strategy as part of the Australian Government's support to the Pacific.
official.program_type: Australian Government postgraduate research scholarship (ACIAR PASS Program), administered at Fiji National University
official.english_requirement: No IELTS or TOEFL score is published. The medium of instruction at FNU is the English language; students must be sufficiently fluent in English to pursue the HDR Programme, and HDR students will provide evidence from undergraduate qualifications or other English qualifications confirming their English language competency. The application form records English language proficiency as either 'Previous program taught in English' or 'IELTS test scores'.

not_confirmed: travel coverage: no travel, airfare or relocation allowance is published for the scholar (only research-related travel inside the research grant)
IELTS/TOEFL minimum score: only general English fluency evidence from prior qualifications is specified

applicant_utility.summary: This is an Australian Government (ACIAR) funded full-tuition research scholarship at Fiji National University, worth FJD 21,450 a year in living allowance plus book, establishment and medical insurance, and a research grant of up to FJD 17,500 (Masters) or FJD 40,000 (PhD). You cannot apply cold: you must first pick a topic from the PASS Compendium of Research Topics, convince the matching FNU supervisor and ACIAR co-supervisor to back it, and have both sign your research intent. Everything is emailed to the ACIAR Graduate Officer as one PDF (plus a separate research-intent PDF) by 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026, so the practical deadline is several weeks earlier than that in supervisor-negotiation time. If you are a citizen of Fiji, Kiribati, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu or Vanuatu with a research degree pathway in agriculture, forestry or fisheries, this is one of the few fully funded routes that lets you stay in the Pacific.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Citizens of the seven ACIAR Pacific partner countries, aged 35 or under (Masters) or 45 or under (PhD), with a strong agriculture, forestry or fisheries degree who want funded research training at FNU without leaving the Pacific.
application_readiness_checklist: Email aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj before anything else to confirm your citizenship, age and GPA against the specific FNU entry route you intend to use

Open the PASS Compendium of Research Topics for 2027 and shortlist two or three topics, then contact the named FNU supervisor and ACIAR co-supervisor early - supervisor agreement is the long pole in this process
Agree the topic in writing, then draft the research intent and budget on the official template and get it signed by both supervisors
Order certified (not plain photocopied) transcripts and certificates now, plus your passport biodata page and birth certificate, and refresh your CV
Brief your two referees so their written references arrive in time - they must be professional, not relatives
If you are a public sector employee, request the Public Service Commission release letter well in advance
Assemble the PDF in the prescribed order (application form, transcripts, certificates, letters of support, birth certificate/passport) and name it exactly PASS2027-your name-FNU-program
Complete the AI-use declaration honestly on the form before signing and dating the declaration
common_rejection_risks: Submitting an unsigned research intent, or one signed by only the FNU supervisor, rather than both the FNU supervisor and the ACIAR co-supervisor
Choosing a topic that is not in the 2027 Compendium, or that is not aligned to an ACIAR project, so the panel cannot see the project fit
Incomplete applications - the FAQs state plainly that incomplete applications will not be considered, and a missing certified transcript, birth certificate, passport page or CV is enough
Missing the 5pm FJT cut-off on 21 October 2026; there is no portal buffer, only an email that either arrives or does not
Failing the age or GPA thresholds without pre-checking eligibility, or for a coursework Masters PhD entry, lacking the separate research methods course
Undisclosed or substantive AI use in the essays, CV or research intent - misuse can be treated as plagiarism or fraud and is a stated disqualification risk
Public sector applicants arriving without the Public Service Commission release letter for the full scholarship term
Sending fragmented attachments or an incorrectly named file, which slows processing and can leave the bundle incomplete
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package does not fund your relocation to Fiji: airfares and other travel to take up the award, visa and migration costs, and settling-in costs beyond the one-off FJD 1,900 establishment allowance are yours to meet. Family costs above the accompanied living allowance rate of FJD 32,472 a year, and research spending above the FJD 17,500 / FJD 40,000 grant cap, also fall to you.
document_audit: Transcripts and certificates must be certified copies - ordinary scans of informal records are the most common gap
The application bundle and the research intent are TWO separate PDFs with different naming conventions; applicants routinely merge them into one
Two referee written references are required, and referees must be professional contacts, not family or relatives
The application form carries an AI-use question and declaration that must be answered and signed, not left blank
The form's checklist also asks for a CV and the biodata page of your passport, which are easy to overlook because the eligibility list never mentions them
alerts: The cut-off is 5pm FJT (Fiji is UTC+12) - applicants emailing from other Pacific countries must convert and send well inside the day

There is effectively one round a year: applications opened 20 August 2026 and close 21 October 2026, with outcomes only advised in late November/early December 2026, so a rejection leaves a long wait before the next cycle
You may not take paid employment while enrolled without the express permission of your supervisor and the head of the relevant school
The published allowances are described as indicative and dependent on your personal circumstances, so confirm your actual entitlement with the ACIAR Graduate Officer
Zoom information sessions run during the application window (Q&A, meet-the-supervisors, research proposal workshop) - attending is the cheapest way to fix a weak topic early
ACIAR's own aciar.gov.au/scholarships/pass page could not be reached during verification, so rely on the FNU PASS pages and the 2027 forms and FAQs for the authoritative figures
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Pre-clear eligibility by email, secure the Compendium topic and dual supervisor sign-off, then email one bundled application PDF plus a separate signed research-intent PDF to aciar-go@fnu.ac.fj with the subject line 'ACIAR Scholarships 2027' before 5pm FJT on 21 October 2026.
